blurb: A lambda parameter written as a record pattern already names its type, in `Item { … }`, and its names take their types from that record, so a `: Type` after the pattern is refused. Remove the annotation; the fix is machine-applicable, so `bynk check --fix` applies it.
example:
items.map((Item { qty, .. }: Item) => qty)    // ✗ the pattern names the type
items.map((Item { qty, .. }) => qty)          // ✓
summary: A lambda parameter with a record pattern carries a type annotation; the pattern's type name already gives the parameter's type.
